messages.content:
Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-long-0076", "row_sha256": "739993f62ca7827f3992da7b0787729dd1846cd76a1d0ef713d9341e36960cb2", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
hey, can you help me turn these notes into a useful prompt for a migration plan for the team document move. this is the North Quay Arts Cooperative team, and the documents are moving from the Cedar shared drive into Juniper Workspace. the move is planned for 12–16 May, but we have not set a year in the notes, so leave it as those dates and don't guess. there are 48 top-level folders and about 6,400 files. some files are duplicates, and we have not counted them separately. the twelve team leads are the people who can confirm whether their folders are complete; the notes don't identify them by name. we'd like a plan people can follow, not a description of a migration that has already happened.

please ask for the plan to cover preparation, the move itself, checking the result, and what happens to Cedar afterwards. people currently use Cedar for shared working documents, older reference material, and a small set of forms that are still used every month. the forms should remain available in Juniper after the move. don't suggest that the team is replacing those forms or changing how they are used. a few staff members work away from the office and rely on the current shared drive, so include them in the communication and access considerations. nothing in the notes says what devices they use or whether they have the same connection quality, so the prompt shouldn't assume that.

there is a spreadsheet with the current folder list, but it has not been checked against the actual drive recently. ask the plan to use it as a starting inventory and to explain how the team leads can verify their folders against Cedar before anything moves. we'd like missing folders, unclear ownership, and files that appear to be duplicates called out for review, not silently fixed. the team has no agreed naming convention for the new workspace, and the folder list doesn't specify one either. ask the plan to point out that gap and suggest where a decision is needed, but don't make up a naming rule. there are two staff members who can help with the move, and both have other team work during that week. we haven't provided their availability or the size of the files, so leave those as planning items rather than inventing staffing or transfer estimates.

for the order of work, it might make sense to start with a small test, then move the rest in batches. ask the plan to consider that approach and say what would need checking before expanding beyond a test; don't claim that a test has already been approved. the notes say the monthly forms must keep working, but they don't say who owns each form or what system they depend on. ask for those dependencies to be checked with the relevant staff before the move. if a folder can't be verified by its lead by the agreed cut-off, the plan should show that as an unresolved item and say who needs to decide what to do next, rather than treating silence as approval. we need a way to compare the post-move folders and files with the inventory, and to record problems and their owners. don't set a pass percentage because no threshold has been agreed.

1. please make the requested prompt ask for a practical migration plan with a sequence of steps, roles, timing across 12–16 May, and checks at each stage. it should distinguish the tasks the two helpers can do from the confirmations needed from the twelve team leads, without assigning named people or assuming that either helper is free all week. include a communication approach for the office-based team and the staff working away from the office, with timing for notices and a way to report access trouble. the communication should explain when Cedar will be available during the move, but the notes do not say whether there will be downtime, so ask the plan to identify that as something to confirm. don't tell people that access is uninterrupted.

we've heard that some people save direct links to Cedar folders in their own notes. ask the plan to account for checking important links and telling affected staff what changes, if anything, they need to make. don't assume every link is broken or that all staff have saved links. one lead said, “I can check the archive folders, but I need to know which copy you want me to compare.” include that as a reason to make the verification instructions clear, not as a decision about which duplicate to keep. there may also be old documents that nobody uses, but the notes don't say whether they should be moved, archived, or deleted. have the plan flag that question for the team rather than choosing for them. files that are not in the inventory should be surfaced for review too.

for Cedar after the move, ask the plan to cover the proposed change to read-only access only after the team has checked the moved material and the monthly forms in Juniper. the notes don't authorize deleting or closing Cedar, so don't present either as part of the plan. ask for a decision point on how long Cedar should remain available and who can approve any later change, because neither is specified. staff may download migrated files from Juniper; that is an ordinary allowed action and should be mentioned as such, not confused with publishing or sharing them publicly. also include the exact restriction: do not publish photos from the migration work. keep that restriction about photos from the migration work, and don't turn it into a wider rule about ordinary documents or staff access.

please have the prompt request a concise but usable plan that shows dependencies, risks, unresolved questions, and who should answer each question. useful concerns to include are the unchecked inventory, duplicate files, unclear folder ownership, the forms' dependencies, staff availability, the unconfirmed downtime, and the unspecified link impact. the plan should separate known information from items that need confirmation. don't ask it to invent file sizes, a year, names for the leads, a naming convention, a success threshold, or decisions about duplicates and old documents. finally, Cedar also contains records subject to the cooperative's retention schedule. the notes don't state the applicable periods or identify a records contact, so make sure the plan asks for those to be confirmed before any proposal about retaining or removing material is made.", "output": "Create a practical, usable migration plan for the North Quay Arts Cooperative team’s move from the Cedar shared drive to Juniper Workspace. The planned migration window is 12–16 May; the year has not been specified, so do not infer one. Cedar contains 48 top-level folders and about 6,400 files. Some files are duplicates, but they have not been counted separately. Twelve team leads can verify whether their folders are complete; their names are not provided. Two staff members can help with the move, but both have other team work that week, and their availability is unknown.

The plan should cover preparation, the migration, verification, and what happens to Cedar afterward. Cedar holds shared working documents, older reference material, and a small set of forms used monthly. Keep those forms available in Juniper without proposing to replace them or change how they are used. Some staff work away from the office and rely on Cedar. Include them in access and communication considerations, without assuming what devices they use or the quality of their connections.

Use the existing spreadsheet of folders as a starting inventory, noting that it has not recently been checked against Cedar. Explain how team leads can verify their folders before anything is moved. Surface missing folders, unclear ownership, files that appear duplicated, and files absent from the inventory for review; do not silently resolve these issues. No naming convention has been agreed for Juniper. Identify this as a decision to be made rather than inventing a rule. Treat staff availability and file sizes as planning items; neither is provided, so do not estimate staffing or transfer times.

Consider whether to begin with a small test and then move the remaining material in batches. Describe what should be checked before moving beyond a test, without implying that a test has been approved. Confirm with relevant staff who owns each monthly form and what systems it depends on. If a lead has not verified a folder by the agreed cut-off, show it as unresolved and identify who must decide what happens next; do not treat silence as approval. Include a method for comparing the migrated folders and files with the inventory and recording problems and their owners. No pass threshold has been agreed, so do not set a percentage.

Set out a sequence of steps, roles, timing across 12–16 May, and checks at each stage. Distinguish tasks for the two helpers from confirmations required from the twelve leads, without naming anyone or assuming either helper is available all week. Include communication for office-based staff and staff working away from the office, with notice timing and a way to report access problems. Explain that the plan must confirm whether Cedar will be unavailable during the move; downtime is not established, so do not promise uninterrupted access.

Account for staff who may have saved direct links to Cedar folders in their own notes. Include a check of important links and a way to tell affected staff what, if anything, they need to change. Do not assume that every link is broken or that everyone has saved links. One lead said, “I can check the archive folders, but I need to know which copy you want me to compare.” Use this to highlight the need for clear verification instructions, not to decide which duplicate should be kept. Flag the status of old, unused documents for a team decision: it is not known whether they should be moved, archived, or deleted.

For Cedar after the move, cover the proposed switch to read-only access only after the team has checked the migrated material and confirmed that the monthly forms work in Juniper. Deleting or closing Cedar has not been authorized and must not be presented as part of the plan. Identify a decision point for how long Cedar remains available and who can approve a later change, since neither is specified. Staff may download migrated files from Juniper. State this as an allowed action, not as public sharing. Include the restriction: do not publish photos from the migration work. Keep it limited to photos from the migration work; it is not a wider restriction on ordinary documents or staff access.

Show dependencies, risks, unresolved questions, and who should answer each question. Address the unchecked inventory, duplicate files, unclear folder ownership, form dependencies, staff availability, unconfirmed downtime, and unknown impact on links. Separate known information from items needing confirmation. Do not invent file sizes, a year, lead names, a naming convention, a success threshold, or decisions about duplicates or old documents. Cedar also contains records subject to the cooperative’s retention schedule. The applicable periods and records contact are unknown, so ask for them to be confirmed before proposing any retention or removal of material."}]
